title: The Chernobyl disaster (1986)
subtitle: April 26, 1986
subject: sciences
description: On April 26, 1986, reactor No. 4 at Chernobyl exploded. It is the most serious civil nuclear accident in history. Here's what happened, without sensationalism.

hero.hook: One night in April 1986, a security test turned into a disaster. The whole of Europe will suffer the fallout.

blocks.text: **April 26, 1986**, at 1:23 a.m., reactor no. 4 of the **Chernobyl power plant**, then in Soviet Ukraine, was the scene of the most serious civilian nuclear accident known. On the  scale, which ranks nuclear events from 1 to 7, it reaches the maximum level, like Fukushima in 2011. [[INES]]

Radioactive materials are released into the atmosphere. The cloud crosses a large part of Europe. Beyond the human drama, Chernobyl permanently changes the way we look at nuclear energy and reveals the flaws in the Soviet system.

It all starts with a security test. Engineers want to check whether, in the event of a power outage, the still-rotating turbines can power the cooling pumps while the diesel generators start up. The idea is good. The conditions of the test are not.

blocks.caption: The containment dome of Reactor No. 4, surrounded by the abandoned buildings of Pripyat.

blocks.text: The night shift works at low power. However, the , a water-cooled and graphite-moderated model, then becomes very unstable. In this type of reactor, the formation of steam bubbles can accelerate the reaction instead of slowing it down. [[The Soviet RBMK reactor]]

When the operator activates the emergency stop, the control bars, intended to stop the reaction, first cause a brief surge due to their design. The power is racing. The steam makes the heart explode. The protection slab, weighing approximately **1,000 tons**, is projected. The reactor is in the open air.
In the basement, a nuclear magma nicknamed the “Elephant’s Foot” was formed. In 1986, going too close to it for too long was fatal within days.

In the first hours, many believed it was a simple roof fire. Firefighters intervene without appropriate protection. Some people handle radioactive graphite without knowing it. The symptoms of acute radiation syndrome appear quickly: nausea, burning.

The neighboring town of **Pripyat**, built for the employees of the power plant, continues its normal life for approximately **36 hours**. The children are playing outside. It was not until **April 27** that its **50,000** inhabitants were evacuated within a few hours, often without being able to take much of anything.

To contain the disaster, the USSR mobilized nearly **600,000** people: the . Helicopter pilots, workers, soldiers. Some only have a few tens of seconds on the roof to clear debris: the electronic robots break down under the radiation. [[liquidators]]
Some liquidators received a medal showing a drop of blood crossed by rays. A rare decoration, created for an invisible danger.

The cloud notably deposits radioactive iodine and cesium over vast areas. The WHO recognizes approximately **4,000** cases of thyroid cancer, especially in children exposed through contaminated milk. The total toll of long-term related deaths remains debated depending on the studies.

Around the site, a  was evacuated. Forty years later, without agriculture or cities, wildlife is often abundant there: wolves, elk, Przewalski's horses. Radioactivity remains a danger, but the human absence has paradoxically left room for nature. [[The 30 km exclusion zone]]

In 1986, a first concrete sarcophagus isolated the reactor. Weakened, it is covered in **2016** by an immense steel arch, the New Safety Containment, designed to last approximately **100 years** and assembled then slid to limit worker exposure.

For , then leader of the USSR, Chernobyl exposed bureaucratic secrecy and industrial negligence. The accident pushes for more transparency (Glasnost) and accelerates the crisis of the Soviet regime. [[Mikhail Gorbachev]]

Throughout the world, the idea of ​​nuclear power without serious risk is shaken. In **1989** the  was born, the World Association of Nuclear Operators, to share good safety practices between countries. Several states are slowing down or reviewing their programs. [[WANO]]

Chernobyl (1986) remains the symbol of a major nuclear accident: technical fault, human errors and opacity. The exclusion zone remains uninhabited, while global nuclear security has had to reinvent itself.
